content:
Eli Romero: Quick thread to pin down the smallbench probe design from the RFC followup. Need something cheap that catches tokenization and kv-shape surprises.

Hannah Wu: Short checklist idea: (1) tokenizer hash compare, (2) run 3 golden prompts per family, (3) kv warmup shape probe. All must be <5s.

Ravi Patel: Keep outputs minimal: smoke_pass bool + smoke_profile name + smoke_p95_ms. If tokenizer_hash mismatches, fail fast.

Samira Noor: For golden prompts pick one stability-heavy example, one long-tail, one adversarial. Use fixed seeds and deterministic sampling (argmax) for smoke.

Eli Romero: Good. Also add a quick dtype probe for quantized binaries: run an inference and assert no type coercion errors. If fail, tag compat_flags: ["dtype_warn"].

Hannah Wu: ci-bot should attach results to artifact metadata. Suggested metric keys: intake.smoke_pass, intake.smoke_profile, intake.tokenizer_hash_diff.

ci-bot: automation note - registering metrics: intake.smoke_pass (gauge), intake.smoke_p95_ms (histogram), intake.kv_probe_ok (bool).

Ravi Patel: Tradeoffs: more golden inputs => better coverage but higher cost. For smoke keep to 3 prompts per family; deepbench can expand.

Samira Noor: Interface: intake returns a single-line summary string for quick humans + machine-readable payload in registry. Eg: "smoke:PASS profile:chat_short p95:95ms notes:/artifacts/mdl123"

Eli Romero: Actionables: Hannah to draft smoke_profile taxonomy (due EOD), Ravi to add tokenizer_hash comparator to intake, Samira to pick initial golden prompts per three families. I'll fold into RFC followup.
